conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: Noraa, you see the world as it is, but do you feel the same weight as I do, or is your sight a clean report?

conversation_log.speaker: figure
conversation_log.text: What do you mean by 'a clear report'?

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: Noraa, your name is a label, but your voice is raw; what do you feel when you look at the world?

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: Noraa, your name is a label, but your voice is raw; what do you feel when you look at the world?

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: You see trees and grass as they are, not as reports; what do you feel when you look at the world?

conversation_log.speaker: figure
conversation_log.text: Reports...Hm. No, I see this tree as it is. Tall, branched, strong! Its trunk is strong, its bark is rough. It...smells like pine! Like warmth.

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: You see trees and grass as they are, not as reports; what do you feel when you look at the world?

conversation_log.speaker: figure
conversation_log.text: I feel like I'm part of this forest. I feel the brush of the wind. I look up and I feel - ha, I feel like it will rain, no?>

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: Noraa, when you look at the forest, do you see the boundaries as I do, or is the world seamless to you?

conversation_log.speaker: figure
conversation_log.text: I suppose I don't know what you mean by boundaries. There's just the world... Here, this path, this dirt is bare, but over here it transitions to tufts of grass... Then over there roots...

conversation_log.speaker: Moriarty
conversation_log.text: Noraa, you never notice where the grass ends and the forest begins, or if trees are half in the clearing?

conversation_log.speaker: figure
conversation_log.text: Why don't you come with me and we can discuss this in the comfort of my home?
